text: Boliney, officially known as the Municipality of Boliney (Ilocano: Ili ti Boliney; Filipino: Bayan ng Boliney), is a municipality in the province of Abra, Philippines. According to the 2024 census, it has a population of 3,778 people. The municipality covers a land area of 216.92 square kilometres (83.75 sq mi), which constitutes 5.21% of Abra’s total area of 4,165.25 square kilometres (1,608.21 sq mi). It is bordered to the north by Sallapadan, Bucloc, and Daguioman, to the east by Tubo and the provinces of Kalinga and Mountain Province, and to the west by Luba and Manabo. Boliney is located 52.93 kilometres (32.89 mi) from the provincial capital Bangued and 422.00 kilometres (262.22 mi) from Manila. The municipality is politically subdivided into 8 barangays, each consisting of puroks and some having sitios. The population density is 17 inhabitants per square kilometre (44/sq mi). The residents are primarily of Cordillera sub-tribes, including the Masadiit of the Tingguian Tribes, Belwang of the Igorot, and Balatoc of the Kalinga tribe, with descendants of other Tinguian sub-tribes such as Binongan, Banao, Maeng, and Ammotan (now called Muyadan of Manabo) also present. The main livelihood of the people comes from rice terraces, though most rice lands were severely damaged or lost due to landslides, mud piles, and the killer quakes in 1990 and 1992; they now obtain most of their rice from Bangued and receive some from other mountain municipalities. Rehabilitation efforts for communal facilities such as roads, trails, irrigation systems, footbridges, and rice fields have been carried out by the Masadiit Farmers Cooperative Inc. (MFCI) with a fund of ₱2,903 million from the Presidential Management Staff, and by the Inter NGO Disaster Relief Services (INDRS) with C$292,516.00 and ₱7 million from Oxfam. Boliney is part of the lone congressional district of Abra and is governed by a mayor as its local chief executive and a municipal council as its legislative body, in accordance with the Local Government Code. The mayor, vice mayor, and councilors are elected directly by the people every three years. The municipality is situated 52.93 kilometres (32.89 mi) from Bangued and is accessible by road, which was completed in 1974; prior to that, access was only possible via a 24-kilometre (15 mi) mountain trail. After 1974, the road was extended by about 14 kilometres (8.7 mi) to reach Danac, the farthest barangay; the current road extends to the Poblacion, while the rest has been abandoned. The Boliney Schools District Office oversees all educational institutions within the municipality, managing and operating both public and private schools from primary to secondary levels.
